rationale: Vozinha left Chaves when his contract expired (June 30) after World Cup heroics; on June 24 reports say three Brazilian Serie B clubs are in talks (one in the Northeast, strongly keen), Athletic (MG) is monitoring, and Ceará declared its own offer dead; a large-market name (Corinthians/Vasco) could hijack a social-media-driven move, so it stays spread.

Liverpool's opening bid was rejected (≈£78-86m) but the club will go to €100m+, personal terms with Diomande are reported agreed and PSG stepped back over price; Leipzig want ~€130m, which is the main obstacle, so the chance he stays or goes elsewhere remains real.

Salah is a free agent deciding after the World Cup; the Saudi Pro League is the persistent favourite with Al-Ittihad the most-cited club (Marib Press reported initial approval in June), Fenerbahçe has talked personally and offered $35m a season, and MLS (San Diego) and Turkish rivals are fallbacks.

Palmeiras is reluctant to sell but faces European pressure: Napoli has had two bids rejected and is sounding them out again, Newcastle reportedly prepared a ~€46m package to formalise when the mid-year window opens July 20, and Liverpool/Man City/Arsenal are monitoring (Palmeiras' president wants to hold him at least until the end of the year, raising the chance no deal happens).

The only concrete suitor is Como, which opened formal talks on June 16 but is waiting on its Cruzeiro Kaiki deal; no other named club yet, so the assignment leaves room for a plausible move abroad not to happen or for an unheralded Ligue 1/Serie A club.

Jackson returns to Chelsea after Bayern declined the €65m option; Chelsea's stated plan is to give Xabi Alonso a look (which would void the question), but several PL/European and Saudi clubs have enquired and AC Milan is the most-linked; Premier League and Saudi buyers are the fallback.

Barcola has told PSG he wants out and remains stalled on a new contract; Arsenal are reportedly preparing a bid and are ahead of Liverpool, while Liverpool made a renewed approach (Diomande and Barcola are both being worked on rather than one replacing the other); PSG is open to a sale at the right price.
Martinez has verbally agreed a 3-year Juventus contract, is looking for a house in Turin, and Villa dropped its asking price to €10m plus bonuses by June 24; Inter and Saudi clubs are fallbacks.

Fernandez wants Real Madrid and has agreed personal terms (contract to 2032); Real is ready to pay €120m+ while Chelsea seek €120-140m and may keep him, but Real is the heavy favourite with City the only second option widely linked.

Arsenal is buying a left winger and Martinelli is available (~£39-45m), so a sale is likely but very much in play; Bayern (needs wing depth after losing Gordon) and PSG (if Barcola leaves) lead, with Barcelona and Atletico long-term admirers, and Martinelli could also stay if Arsenal keeps him. Arsenal staying is included as an outcome only because the question names Martinelli's club, not a transfer club; scoring is unaffected.

Arsenal cut Jesus's asking price to £20-25m and want him off the wage bill; Everton's long-standing interest has not produced a bid, Palmeiras (his former club) has signalled interest, and Atletico, Juventus and Milan have enquired, so the likely destination is spread across Everton and Palmeiras.

The biggest completed PL inbound is Jeremy Jacquet (£55m, Liverpool); Man City are pushing a ~£100-125m deal for Elliot Anderson, which would already top the window, and Liverpool's €100m+ pursuit of Diomande and Arsenal/Liverpool interest in Barcola (£60-105m) are the other routes to the highest fee.
